artist_statement.text:
‘the cost of open’


before 2023, visitors lined up through the night hoping to secure one of the limited parking spots at moraine lake. after years of congestion, environmental strain, and thousands of vehicles being turned away daily, parks canada closed the road to private vehicles and replaced access with a timed shuttle and reservation system.

the landscape itself remains open and public, but entry is now mediated through reservations, ticketing, and scheduled transit. this photograph sits inside that shift where gates increasingly exist to protect the very thing we want to keep open to all. it solved the problem of capacity crisis and environmental strain, but created another problem: who can actually afford to go?


shot on Nikon D850

f/8, ISO 400, 1/400 sec

processed in adobe lightroom 

10080 × 5670 pixels 


location: moraine lake, canada 

year: 2024
